title: Storage Retention Catalog
description: Single source of truth for storage retention (AL-01). Each entry declares, for one repo-relative directory, what class of artifact lives there, how long it is retained (ttl_days), and what happens on expiry (action). Consumed by libs/core/storage-retention-catalog.ts, which falls back to built-in defaults mirroring the pre-catalog constants when this file is missing or invalid — the janitor never dies because of a bad catalog. Entries without ttl_days are note-only declarations (e.g. self-expiring stores); directories with no entry at all are never deleted and, under active/shared/runtime/, are surfaced by the janitor report as uncovered.

version.description: Semver of this catalog format. Bump minor for additive vocabulary, major for a change to enforcement semantics.

description.description: Free-text human note describing the intent of this catalog.

entries.description: Retention declarations. Paths must be unique (enforced by the loader).

path.description: Repo-relative directory governed by this rule (POSIX separators, no leading/trailing slash, no '..').

artifact_class.description: What kind of artifact the directory holds. evidence = execution/audit evidence; report = generated reports; export = outbound deliverables; cache = regenerable intermediates; tmp = consumable scratch; log = append-only logs.

ttl_days.description: Retention period in days, evaluated against file mtime. Omit for note-only entries whose contents self-expire (the note must explain the mechanism).

action.description: What the janitor does when the TTL elapses. delete = remove the file; archive = move it to the archive tree (reserved for AL-03+; current enforcement only implements delete).

audit.description: When true, expiry actions must leave an audit record.

note.description: Human rationale: why this TTL/action, and any special expiry mechanism.
